title: an unrecognized `scatter_policy` value is rejected, and the specific dead spelling used here stays rejected forever
why: `scatter_policy` declares the contract for how a block's terminal write
behaves — what the committed result means — so an unrecognized value must
be refused rather than let the executor guess.
The rejected value here is `unique_target`, a spelling that was proposed by
mistake early on and overturned before any code used it. This fixture
pins that a loader must never accept that spelling: a loader that
'helpfully' accepts it as a synonym for the real value fails here, in both
The fixture is otherwise identical to row01's golden with only this one
field changed, so the only thing that can make it reject is this
The manifest-bypassing plugin loader is exercised too, since its only
structural gate is the shared validator.
